open_questions.question: Does 'builder' mean the agent holding the task when it moved to completed, or every agent that ran on it? Resolved by the operator 2026-11-11: the holder at completion.

problem:
The facts that matter most about a task are hidden inside it. The operator cannot tell from the board whether approved work is already on main, still being checked, or failed to land, so they cannot decide whether it is time to test or restart. The project does not matter: this applies to any project, not only AgentWeave.
- Landing state (queued, checking, landing, held, landed, not_landed, sent_back; TaskLanding model) is shown only in the drawer (TaskDetailDrawer.tsx:701).
- An approved task looks the same whether it is on main or not.
- A task stuck for days looks the same as one that moved a minute ago.
- When a task goes to review, `assignee` is overwritten with the reviewer (api/v1/tasks.py:2471; mender.py:321). The `builder` column is only set inside a build and names who was meant to build, not who did (models.py:913). So the developer's name disappears.
- The working marker is wrong today; AW-94 fixes it, and this slice relies on that fix.

The operator rejected a "safe to restart" indicator on 2026-11-11: it would be AgentWeave-specific. The aim is clarity about each task, so the operator can draw that conclusion for any project.

requirements.statement: Every task card shows exactly one stage, readable without opening the task. The stages are: not started; being worked on; waiting for an answer or blocked; waiting for review; under review; sent back; approved, waiting to land; checking; landing; on main; landing held; did not land; closed without landing.

requirements.rationale: The status 'approved' says a reviewer agreed. It does not say the work reached main, and those are the moments the operator needs to tell apart.
requirements.statement: A card's stage reflects what is actually happening, not only the task's status column. A task is 'being worked on' only while a run bound to that task is running. It is 'on main' only once its work has landed on the main branch. An approved task whose work has not landed is never shown as on main.
A card at 'on main' shows the short commit id its work landed at. A card at 'landing held' shows what it waits on. A card at 'did not land' shows why, in one line.

requirements.rationale: A task stuck for days must look different from one that moved a minute ago; nothing on the card shows that today.
requirements.statement: Every card shows how long its task has been at its current stage, measured from when it entered that stage, in a compact form ('14 min', '2 days'). The duration advances while the board is open, at least once a minute.

When a task is waiting (for an answer, blocked, held, or not started because of prerequisites), its card names what it waits on in one line. That is one of: the agent whose question is open, the id of each unfinished task it depends on, or the name of the failing check or held item. A task not waiting shows no such line.
On the board, a task that is on main is visually distinct from an approved task not yet on main. The operator can tell them apart without reading the stage text.
Without opening any task, the board shows how many tasks are approved but not yet on main, and lets the operator see which ones. The same applies to tasks being worked on.

A card's stage, its waits-on line and the counts from not-yet-on-main change within 5 seconds of the underlying change (a run ending, a landing finishing, a prerequisite completing), without a page reload.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-11: one clear name, the holder at completion, rather than every agent that ran on the task.
requirements.statement: When a task moves to completed, it records as its builder the agent holding it at that moment. That name stays unchanged when the task is handed to a reviewer or tester, inside or outside a flow. If the task is sent back and completed again, the builder becomes whoever holds it at that later completion.
From 'waiting for review' onward, a card and the task drawer show the builder and the current reviewer as two separately labelled names. A task never reviewed shows only its builder.

in_scope: A true stage on every card, through landing on main, with time at stage and what it waits on
Board-level view of what is not yet on main and what is being worked on
Recording and showing the builder separately from the reviewer
non_goals: Any 'safe to restart' indicator or other AgentWeave-specific readiness signal (operator, 2026-11-11)
Changing how landing itself works (queue, checks, batching)
Moving tasks outside a flow (slice loose-tasks)
Hiding finished tasks and the spec tag on cards (slice finding)
The failing-checks marker and the visual redesign beyond what showing these stages needs (slice redesign)
The working-marker bug itself (AW-94); this slice builds on its fix

summary: Every card on the board shows the stage its task has really reached, all the way to "on main", how long it has been there, what it waits on, who built it and who is reviewing it. The board separates work on main from approved work still on its way. From this the operator can work out, for any project, whether it is time to test, merge or restart, without opening a task.
